write_status: reviewed-only; no production insert authorized until both Commons images are localized, metadata is synchronized, and guarded migration passes isolated PostgreSQL dry-run
review_method: Confirmed project identity, location, year, architect and mixed retail/residential program against the architects' current first-party project pages.
Queried Commons through the MediaWiki API for exact file dimensions, authorship, own-work or Flickr provenance, and license, then manually inspected both images.
Queried production architects, buildings and graduation profiles without writing data; found only the existing MVRDV architect and no target building or CASE profile conflicts.

Used retail as the fine primary function while preserving mixed-use as the broad building type; Markthal also receives public-space because MVRDV explicitly describes the covered market square as public space.

architect.name_ja: クライン・ダイサム・アーキテクツ

identity_evidence: Klein Dytham architecture identifies Daikanyama T-SITE as its project in Daikanyama, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo and lists the principal use as retail and apartments.
The official project page states that the campus-like Tsutaya complex opened to the public in December 2011 and credits architecture and interior design to Klein Dytham architecture.

image.visual_evidence: The image clearly shows the exact low-rise T-SITE retail volumes, glazed interiors, pedestrian court and active evening use.
image.rights_evidence: MediaWiki reports Jonathan Lin, links the original Flickr work, and identifies CC BY-SA 2.0.

canonical_building.name_ja: ロッテルダム・マルクトハル

identity_evidence: MVRDV identifies Markthal as a realised Rotterdam project completed in 2014, combining food, leisure, living and parking.
The official project page lists retail and residential programs and describes the central market hall as a covered public square beneath the apartment arch.

image.visual_evidence: The image clearly shows the exact glazed market-hall entrance, occupied apartment arch, interior artwork and market units; the adjacent Pencil building is visible through the hall but is not the image subject.
image.rights_evidence: MediaWiki reports Michielverbeek's own work under CC BY-SA 4.0.
